title: How to remove an email account in Apple Mail on Mac: step by step
metaTitle: Remove an Email Account in Apple Mail on Mac: Steps
description: Learn how to remove an email account in Apple Mail on Mac: open Mail settings, click Remove, and save your messages first.

intro: To remove an email account in Apple Mail on Mac, open Mail and choose Mail > Settings, click Accounts, select the account, and click Remove. Removing it deletes that account's messages from your Mac, but the copies stay on the mail server.
tldr: Move any messages you want to keep into a mailbox under On My Mac before you remove anything.
Choose Mail > Settings, click Accounts, select the account, then click Remove.
If another app uses the account, Mail sends you to System Settings > Internet Accounts to finish.
To hide an account without deleting it, clear its Mail checkbox instead.
Older Mail versions call the menu Preferences, and the steps are otherwise the same.

blocks.text: Removing an account and turning it off are two different jobs. Removing deletes that account's messages from this Mac. Turning it off hides them, and the account stays set up. Pick the one you need before you start, because the steps below cover removal.
Decide what you actually want to happen

Mail gives you three separate actions. They sit in different places, and they change different things. The table shows what each one does to the messages on your Mac. Read it once before you click anything.

rows: Deletes the account's messages from this Mac. Copies stay on the mail server.
Mail > Accounts, then clear the Mail checkbox
Hides the account's messages. Select the checkbox again to bring them back without a fresh download.
System Settings > Internet Accounts > Delete Account
Removes the account and turns off its features in all apps. Apple warns it can remove data stored in your apps, which may return if you add the account again.
blocks.caption: Three ways to stop using an account in Mail on Mac, with menu paths from Apple's guides.

blocks.text: Save the messages you want to keep first

Apple's guide tells you to move or copy messages you want to keep into a mailbox under On My Mac before you remove the account. Mailboxes under On My Mac stay on this Mac after the account is gone. Mailboxes that belong to the account are removed from this Mac with it.

items: Click the account's Inbox or the folder that holds the messages you want.
Command-click each message you want to keep, so they all stay selected.
Drag the selection onto a mailbox under On My Mac in the sidebar.
Open that On My Mac mailbox and confirm the messages are there.

blocks.text: Then check the server side. Apple's troubleshooting page suggests testing the account in webmail. For iCloud Mail, that means iCloud.com. If your messages show up there, the server still has them. If they don't, sort that out before you remove anything.
Settings or Preferences: which label your Mac shows

Apple's main guide says Mail > Settings, then Accounts. Apple's older 13.0 guide says Mail > Preferences > Accounts for removal, and it uses Mail > Accounts to turn an account off. That guide doesn't explain the difference. Use the label your menu shows, because the steps after it stay the same. I could not confirm which label the newest Mail build uses, so check your menu before you follow the path word for word.
When another app still uses the account

Mail doesn't always finish the job on its own. If an app such as Calendar or Contacts uses the account, Mail prompts you to handle it in Internet Accounts. In System Settings, Internet Accounts sits in the sidebar, and you may need to scroll to find it. Select the account there to see your options.

You have two choices in that pane. Deselect Mail to keep the account for other apps. Or click Delete Account to remove the account and turn off all of its features. Apple warns that this can remove data stored in your apps. That data may come back if you add the account again, so decide before you click.
Turn off an account without deleting it

Turning off is the safer choice when you're unsure. Open Mail > Accounts, then clear the Mail checkbox next to the account. Mail hides its messages. Select the checkbox again later, and the messages return without a fresh download from the server. This works well when you want a break from one inbox.
Why a removed account comes back

Some people remove an account and watch it reappear a minute or two later. Apple's support pages don't list that as a known problem. One Apple Community thread from a Monterey 12.7.4 user describes it. The suggested fixes in that thread were Internet Accounts, Mail > Settings > Accounts, and backing up messages first.

The original poster said the Internet Accounts step did not help. Signing out of iCloud on their iMac solved it. That is one report from one person on one version. Check the Internet Accounts pane and your iCloud settings to see whether the account is still attached somewhere. Don't sign out of iCloud on a Mac you rely on without knowing what else depends on it.
Password prompts and full mailboxes

Apple's troubleshooting page offers a simple fix for many account problems. Remove the account, add it again, and choose the correct provider. Apple also has a separate article for Mail that keeps asking for a password. Search Apple's support site for that article if the prompts continue after you re-add the account.

A full mailbox can stop an account from working, and Apple gives a path for that. Control-click the mailbox, choose Get Account Info, and delete the messages you no longer need. Then choose Mailbox > Erase Deleted Items. You can also move messages to On My Mac. Do this before you remove the account, so you don't lose messages you wanted.
Mistakes people make when they remove an account

items: Removing the account before moving messages to On My Mac.
Clicking Remove when they only wanted to hide the account. The Mail checkbox does that job.
Forgetting the Internet Accounts step, so the account stays active in Calendar or Contacts.
Choosing Delete Account without reading Apple's warning that it can remove data stored in your apps.
Assuming the job is done after one click. Check the Accounts list again, and look in Internet Accounts too.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts for this task

Apple's Mail keyboard shortcut page lists about 30 shortcuts for composing, replying, moving, and archiving mail. None of them opens Settings or Accounts, and none removes an account. You'll click through the menus for this task. Some third-party guides mention ⌘, for Settings. Apple's pages don't confirm it, so test it yourself before you rely on it.
Check that the account is gone

Look in three places. First, the Accounts list in Mail should not show the account. Second, the Mail sidebar should no longer list its mailboxes. Third, Internet Accounts in System Settings should not show it, unless you chose Deselect Mail on purpose. Then open your On My Mac mailbox and confirm the messages you saved are still there.
Which Mail version these steps cover

I could not run these steps on a Mac while writing this page. Apple's guide pages don't label the macOS or Mail version they cover. Some of Apple's URLs point to macOS 27 and Mail 16.0, but the pages don't say so in plain words. Apple's What's new page for Mail 16.0 lists Suggestions, Personalized Writing, and search by meaning. It does not mention changes to the Mail menu, Settings, or Accounts.
What to do after the account is gone

Many people remove an account because they're switching to another one. If you're adding Gmail to this Mac, follow [How to add Gmail to Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/use-gmail-in-apple-mail-in-gmail). That page covers the account setup, so your new inbox starts out tidy.

If your inbox was the reason for the cleanup, try [How to unsubscribe from emails in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/unsubscribe-from-a-mailing-list-in-apple-mail). Blocking a sender is another option, covered in [How to block a sender in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/block-a-sender-in-apple-mail).
Why this question comes up so often

Litmus put Apple Mail at 45.51% of tracked email-client opens in February 2026, according to SellCell's summary of that table. Opens are not the same as users, so read the number as a rough signal. Still, a large share of tracked opens means many Mac owners will meet this task at some point.

faq.question: Does removing an email account delete my emails from the server?
faq.answer: Apple's guide says no. Removing an account in Mail deletes its messages from your Mac, but copies stay on the mail server. Check webmail to confirm your messages are still there before you rely on that.

faq.question: What is the difference between removing and turning off an account?
faq.answer: Removing deletes the account's messages from this Mac. Turning it off, by clearing the Mail checkbox under Mail > Accounts, hides the messages. Select the checkbox again and they return without a fresh download.

faq.question: Will removing the account also remove it from Calendar and Contacts?
faq.answer: Mail sends you to Internet Accounts when another app uses the account. Click Delete Account there to remove it from every app. Apple warns that this can remove data stored in your apps, and it may return if you add the account again.

faq.question: Can I add the account back after I remove it?
faq.answer: Yes. Add it again in Mail or System Settings and choose the correct provider. Apple says data removed with Delete Account may be restored when you add the account again.

faq.question: Why does my removed account keep coming back?
faq.answer: One Apple Community thread from a Monterey 12.7.4 user describes this. The Internet Accounts step did not help that person, and signing out of iCloud fixed it for them. Treat that as one lead, not a known fix.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to remove an account?
faq.answer: Not one that Apple lists. Apple's Mail shortcut page has about 30 shortcuts, and none opens Settings or removes an account. Some third-party guides mention ⌘, for Settings, but Apple's pages don't confirm it.

faq.question: Why does my Mac say Preferences instead of Settings?
faq.answer: Older Mail versions use Mail > Preferences. Apple's 13.0 guide uses that name. Use whichever item your menu shows, because the steps after it match.

faq.question: Do I need to restart my Mac after removing an account?
faq.answer: Apple's troubleshooting page for Mail does not mention restarting. Its advice is to remove the account, add it again with the correct provider, and then test the account in webmail.

task: Remove an email account in Apple Mail on Mac
appliesTo: Apple Mail on Mac, with Mail > Settings or Mail > Preferences menus
requirements: Apple Mail open, with the account already set up
Messages you want to keep, moved to On My Mac first
Webmail login for the provider, to check server copies
System Settings access if another app uses the account

steps.name: Save the messages you want to keep
steps.text: Move or copy the messages you want to keep into a mailbox under On My Mac in the sidebar. Removing the account deletes its messages from this Mac.
steps.tip: Command-click several messages to select them, then drag the group onto the On My Mac mailbox.

steps.name: Open Mail settings
steps.text: Open Mail, then choose Mail > Settings from the menu bar at the top of the screen.
steps.tip: If your menu shows Preferences instead, choose Mail > Preferences. The steps stay the same.

steps.name: Open the Accounts pane
steps.text: Click Accounts. Mail lists every account it uses, so you can pick the one to remove.

steps.name: Select the account you want to remove
steps.text: Click the account once so it's highlighted. Check the email address in its details to be sure you have the right one.
steps.tip: Two accounts from the same provider can look alike, so check the full address.

steps.name: Click Remove
steps.text: Click the Remove button. Some versions show it as a minus sign. Removal deletes the account's messages from this Mac.
steps.tip: Copies stay on the mail server. Check webmail if you need those messages.

steps.name: Handle the Internet Accounts prompt
steps.text: If another app on your Mac uses the account, Mail prompts you to finish in Internet Accounts. Open that pane from System Settings.
steps.tip: Scroll the sidebar if you don't see Internet Accounts right away.

steps.name: Choose Deselect Mail or Delete Account
steps.text: Select the account in Internet Accounts. Deselect Mail to keep the account for other apps, or click Delete Account to remove it from every app.
steps.tip: Apple warns that Delete Account can remove data stored in your apps. Read that warning before you click.

steps.name: Confirm the account is gone
steps.text: Check the Accounts list in Mail and the sidebar. The account and its mailboxes should no longer appear, and your On My Mac messages should still be there.
steps.tip: If the account is still listed after a few minutes, see the troubleshooting section below.

steps.name: Check the server copies
steps.text: Open the provider's webmail, such as iCloud.com for iCloud Mail, and confirm your messages are still there.

troubleshooting.problem: The account reappears a minute or two after removal
troubleshooting.fix: One Apple Community thread from a Monterey 12.7.4 user describes this. Signing out of iCloud fixed it for that poster, but the Internet Accounts step did not. Check Internet Accounts and iCloud settings before you assume that fix applies to you.

troubleshooting.problem: Mail keeps asking for the password
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the account, add it again, and choose the correct provider. Apple also has a separate article for repeated password prompts in Mail, which you can find on Apple's support site.

troubleshooting.problem: The mailbox is over its storage quota
troubleshooting.fix: Control-click the mailbox, choose Get Account Info, and delete messages you no longer need. Then choose Mailbox > Erase Deleted Items, or move messages to On My Mac.

troubleshooting.problem: You can't find the Remove button
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure the account is selected in the Accounts list. Some versions show Remove as a minus sign rather than a word, so look for that before you give up.

troubleshooting.problem: Your menu says Preferences, not Settings
troubleshooting.fix: Older Mail versions use Mail > Preferences. Choose that item and follow the same steps from the Accounts pane.

troubleshooting.problem: You wanted to hide the account, not delete it
troubleshooting.fix: Open Mail > Accounts and clear the Mail checkbox. Your messages come back when you select the checkbox again, without a fresh download.
